captures.q: What are the arguments in “The Summarizer as Horizon of Reception: Machine Composition and the Jaussian Frame” by Lee Sharks? Ground your answer in a reading of the text itself.
captures.description: THE JAUSSIAN FRAME READ IN ORDER, THE FIVE PATTERNS AND THE OBJECT THAT READS BACK: asked for the arguments of The Summarizer as Horizon of Reception: Machine Composition and the Jaussian Frame, grounded in the text, ChatGPT reads #1421 (Goodreads ×7) section by section: the horizon of expectations become infrastructure; reception become composition, centralized and institutionally controlled; the capture method against a self-authored corpus, more than 200 captures from February to July 2026; framework adoption, the attribution-attenuation gradient, provenance erasure and PER, active correction, demand-side signals; the 'anthologizing reader', probabilistic flattening and attribution economics; neither capitulation nor refusal; and the object that 'reads back'. It marks the self-authored corpus as the tracer's strength and its limit.

atoms.evidence: Lee Sharks’s “The Summarizer as Horizon of Reception: Machine Composition and the Jaussian Frame” argues
Lee Sharks’s “The Summarizer as Horizon of Reception: Machine Composition and the Jaussian Frame” argues
The essay’s central move is to reinterpret Hans Robert Jauss’s concept of the horizon of expectations as a computational system that operates between a work and its reader.
The essay begins from a principle associated with reception aesthetics
Its second contribution is methodological: it proposes capturing outputs against a known corpus so that reception becomes empirically inspectable.
The essay acknowledges that this makes the material useful as a tracer but limits how far its findings can be generalized. It presents a method that other researchers could apply
